findings.source_passage: The abnormal mind is quick to detect and attach itself to this quality when it appears in a normal person, and so it came about that in college I was unjustly accused of being a politician
findings.source_locator: Opening section, paragraph 3, between father's advice and 'Reserving judgements'
findings.why_it_matters: This passage is part of the long voice-establishing digression that defines Nick's self-presentation as a reluctant confessor; its removal collapses the ironic self-awareness that frames his role as narrator. The detail about 'feigned sleep' and 'plagiaristic' confidences is distinctive prose that establishes Nick's sardonic register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the passage from 'The abnormal mind is quick to detect' through 'plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions' — it is the ironic machinery behind the 'Reserving judgements' sentence and must precede it.

findings.source_passage: promising to unfold the shining secrets that only Midas and Morgan and Maecenas knew
findings.source_locator: Nick's self-introduction section, after 'like new money from the mint'
findings.why_it_matters: The Midas/Morgan/Maecenas triplet is prosodically distinctive (alliterative, cataloguing) and typifies Nick's literary self-irony; it is the payoff of the 'red and gold like new money from the mint' image. Without it, the optional tagged signature is only half-preserved.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'promising to unfold the shining secrets that only Midas and Morgan and Maecenas knew' immediately after 'like new money from the mint.'

findings.source_passage: It was the kind of voice that the ear follows up and down, as if each speech is an arrangement of notes that will never be played again. Her face was sad and lovely with bright things in it
findings.source_locator: First meeting with Daisy at East Egg, after 'I'm p-paralysed with happiness'
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves this passage, but it does so by dropping the crucial transition: Nick's first-person observation about Daisy's murmur ('I've heard it said that Daisy's murmur was only to make people lean toward her; an irrelevant criticism that made it no less charming') is excised. This is signature ironic commentary on Daisy's seductive technique and foreshadows 'her voice is full of money'; its absence flattens Nick's ironic mediation.
findings.suggested_fix: After 'That was a way she had,' restore: 'She hinted in a murmur that the surname of the balancing girl was Baker. (I've heard it said that Daisy's murmur was only to make people lean toward her; an irrelevant criticism that made it no less charming.)'

findings.source_passage: Two shining arrogant eyes had established dominance over his face and gave him the appearance of always leaning aggressively forward… It was a body capable of enormous leverage—a cruel body.
findings.source_locator: Tom Buchanan's physical introduction, paragraph beginning 'He had changed since his New Haven years'
findings.why_it_matters: The tagged signature is present, but the sentence 'Not even the effeminate swank of his riding clothes could hide the enormous power of that body' and 'there were men at New Haven who had hated his guts' are present in the draft — good. However, the immediately following voice passage — 'Now, don't think my opinion on these matters is final… just because I'm stronger and more of a man than you are… I always had the impression that he approved of me and wanted me to like him with some harsh, defiant wistfulness of his own' — is completely absent. This is interpretively essential: it establishes the psychological dynamic between Nick and Tom that runs through the whole novel.
findings.suggested_fix: After 'There was a touch of paternal contempt in it, even toward people he liked,' restore the indirect-speech passage: '"Now, don't think my opinion on these matters is final," he seemed to say, "just because I'm stronger and more of a man than you are." We were in the same senior society, and while we were never intimate I always had the impression that he approved of me and wanted me to like him with some harsh, defiant wistfulness of his own.'

findings.source_passage: Sometimes she and Miss Baker talked at once, unobtrusively and with a bantering inconsequence that was never quite chatter, that was as cool as their white dresses and their impersonal eyes in the absence of all desire.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is one of the chapter's finest observations on Daisy and Jordan's social affect — 'never quite chatter,' 'impersonal eyes in the absence of all desire' — and it anchors the thematic reading of these women as performing rather than feeling. Its loss is a mild but real voice flattening.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence after the 'Hulking' exchange, before the transition to Nick's 'You make me feel uncivilized' remark or its equivalent.

findings.source_passage: Daisy peremptorily called: 'Wait! I forgot to ask you something, and it's important. We heard you were engaged to a girl out West.'
findings.source_locator: Departure scene, after Nick starts his motor
findings.why_it_matters: The draft summarizes this exchange ('called after me as I started my motor: had I heard I was engaged to a girl out West?') rather than rendering the dialogue. The exchange is brief period-register comedy and the draft's compression into indirect speech loses Daisy's characteristic breathless delivery.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the brief dialogue verbatim — it is only four lines and establishes Daisy's social register clearly; the indirect-summary version is tonally flat.

summary: All verbatim-priority signatures are present and intact; four medium-severity voice and interpretive losses (the 'abnormal mind' narrator digression, the 'Midas and Morgan and Maecenas' payoff, the Daisy-murmur ironic aside, and the Tom psychological-dominance passage) and two low-severity flattenings are found, but no high-severity failures — verdict is a narrow pass that should trigger revision of the medium items before final output.
